body.v: I've moved the notes to a new TeamChat page so everyone can edit them. You may need to sign in again to get to it.
On Wednesday you wrote: "The notes are final, I'll share them after the call."

hotspots.explain: It is Jonas's address, and his thread too. But once an account is hijacked, the address proves nothing.
Jonas usually puts the notes in the shared folder. A new page that makes you sign in again isn't like him. And a real address doesn't prove he is the one writing.
teamchat-signin.example is not TeamChat's domain. Whoever controls Jonas's account can send any link they like.
Quoting your own words fits a real conversation. But anyone with access to the inbox can copy them.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Maybe not Jonas. The address and the thread are genuine, which doesn't rule out a hijacked account. A phone call will settle it.
choices: Definitely Jonas, since the conversation is genuine
A stranger with a near-identical address
Maybe Jonas, maybe someone who hijacked his account

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Wanting to help: a colleague has just made life easier for the whole team, so this is no time to drag your feet.
choices: Wanting to keep up with the team and help

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in again through a link. Your TeamChat login details would go to whoever controls Jonas's account.
choices: Sign in again through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Leave the link alone. Open TeamChat yourself to look for the notes, or call Jonas on the number you already have.
choices: Click, since the conversation is genuine
Reply to ask whether it is really him
Open TeamChat yourself, or call Jonas

actions.label: Open TeamChat yourself to look for the notes, or call Jonas
actions.consequence: No new page in TeamChat. And Jonas never sent that email.

actions.label: Click the link and sign in, since the conversation is genuine
actions.consequence: The fake sign-in page copies your login details for whoever controls the account.

actions.label: Reply: "Is this really you?"
actions.consequence: The intruder says yes, of course. You asked the person holding the account.

actions.label: Tell the IT team or your manager that Jonas's account may have been hijacked
actions.consequence: The account can be locked before it catches other colleagues.

attacker_reveal: Why fake an address when you can borrow the real one? Jonas's account, his thread, your own sentences... You had one way out left: call him.
